title: Enterprise Onboarding & Support Playbook — Health Checks, QBRs, Integration, and Escalation
author: Ava Thompson
content:
Summary:
This playbook consolidates the standard operating procedures for enterprise customer onboarding at Redwood Inference, including integration checkpoints, known issues and workarounds, escalation paths, and the cadence/materials for health checks and Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs). Use this as the canonical reference for Customer Success (CS) and Support teams running onboarding engagements and ongoing operational reviews.

Goals:
- Accelerate time-to-value for enterprise customers while protecting reliability and SLOs.
- Provide clear, repeatable integration and handoff steps for Engineering, CS, and Support.
- Reduce mean time to resolution (MTTR) via a tiered escalation flow and playbooks for common issues.
- Standardize Health Checks and QBR materials to measure success and surface product improvements.

Scope:
This document covers: enterprise onboarding phases (setup -> go-live -> post-live), integration prerequisites, step-by-step onboarding checklist, support and escalation process, recurring health-check cadence and QBR templates, and a curated list of known issues with workarounds. It does not replace security or legal approvals (see Security & Compliance pages).

Ownership & Roles:
- Account Executive (AE): ownership of contract milestones and commercial sign-offs.
- Customer Success Manager (CSM): primary owner of onboarding project plan, QBRs, and health checks.
- Solutions Engineer (SE): technical lead for integration, API-testing, and handoffs to Support.
- Support Engineer (L2/L3): post-go-live incident response and troubleshooting.
- Engineering Pager (on-call): platform incidents requiring code or infra intervention.

Key Contacts (example):
- CSM: csm-<customer>@redwood.ai
- SE: se-<customer>@redwood.ai
- Support: support@redwood.ai (internal routing to L2/L3)
- Pager duty: eng-pager@redwood.ai (follow on-call rota)

Pre-Onboarding Checklist (must complete before integration work begins):
1) Contract & data agreements signed (legal)
2) Customer creates Redwood account and completes org setup
3) Product and SE alignment call scheduled (agenda in Templates section)
4) Network & security requirements documented (VPC peering, IP allowlists, KMS/HSM details)
5) Model selection and expected workload profile (tokens/sec, request size, peak concurrency) entered into onboarding spreadsheet
6) Identify integration type: Hosted API | Dedicated | Private.

Onboarding Phases (high-level):
1. Kickoff (Week 0):
   - Deliverables: Project plan, success criteria, contact matrix.
   - Action: Run the Kickoff agenda, confirm roles, schedule weekly check-ins.
2. Integration & Verification (Weeks 1–3):
   - Deliverables: API keys, network connectivity (if private), basic integration demo, perf baseline.
   - Steps:
     a) Customer integrates SDK/REST into test environment. Example curl test:
        curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" -d '{"model":"redwood-1", "prompt":"hello"}'
     b) Run smoke tests and validate latency and correctness.
     c) SE documents any custom prompts, post-processing, or function-calling patterns.
3. Performance & Load Validation (Week 2–4):
   - Deliverables: Load test report, recommended batching/quantization settings, and cost estimates.
   - Steps: ramp test to expected production QPS, track 50/95/99 P50/P95/P99 latencies, token cost per-request.
4. Go-Live & Monitoring Handoff (Week 4+):
   - Deliverables: Support runbook, alerting subscription, escalation contacts, SLA definitions.
   - Action: Execute canary rollout (10% traffic → 50% → 100%) with rollback plan.
5. Post-Go-Live (0–90 days):
   - Deliverables: Weekly health checks for first 30 days, monthly QBR preparation.

Integration Guide (concise checklist):
- Authentication: API keys rotated per customer policy. For Private, configure mTLS and KMS endpoints.
- Network: Provide allowlist IPs (see table below). If using VPC peering, exchange route-ids and test connectivity.
- Secrets: Use customer-managed KMS where requested; add KMS ARN and key policy to onboarding spreadsheet.
- Model and Routing: If routing rules applied, document fallback model policy and cost tiers.

Example Network Requirements Table (copy into customer doc):
- IPs to allowlist: 52.23.12.0/22, 18.205.0.0/16 (region-specific; SE will confirm)
- Ports: 443 outbound
- VPC peering: request AWS account ID and VPC CIDR
- Expected egress per month: estimate tokens * average token size

Escalation Flow (TL;DR):
- Tier 0: Self-serve docs / status.redwood.ai / FAQs (CSM & customer)
- Tier 1: Customer Support (support@redwood.ai) — respond within 1 business hour for P1/P2, 4 hours for P3
- Tier 2: SE & CSM engagement; workaround implementation and triage — initial contact within 2 hours for P1
- Tier 3: Platform engineering + on-call pager — engaged if incident affects SLOs or requires code/infra changes

Severity Definitions & Target Response Times:
- P0 / Sev 1 (Service down or major customer impact): Response 15 minutes, update cadence 15 minutes, engage Tier 3 immediately.
- P1 / Sev 2 (Degraded service or major feature failure): Response 60 minutes, update cadence 60 minutes, escalate to SE within 2 hours.
- P2 / Sev 3 (Partial impairment, non-critical): Response 4 business hours, workaround within 24 hours.
- P3 / Low (General question / enhancement request): Response 1 business day.

Escalation Steps (numbered):
1) Triage ticket in Zendesk with severity and triage notes.
2) CSM/SE perform reproducer and attach logs (requesting redwood debug bundle if needed):
   redwood-cli collect-logs --org <org_id> --since 1h --output <bundle.zip>
3) If reproducible and impacts SLO -> open internal incident and notify on-call.
4) Communicate status to customer via CSM, include mitigation and ETA.
5) Postmortem for any Sev1/Sev2 incident with RCA and action items within 7 days.

Health Checks & QBRs:
- 30-day health cadence: weekly health check for first 30 days focusing on integration stability, latency and cost.
- 90-day review: assess feature usage, optimize batching/quantization, and present cost savings.
- Quarterly Business Review (QBR) cadence (every 90 days):
  - Owner: CSM with SE support.
  - Agenda: 1) Executive summary, 2) Usage and performance (P50/P95/P99), 3) Cost & optimization opportunities, 4) Product roadmap items relevant to customer, 5) Action items and success metrics.
  - Deliverables: QBR deck (slides), runbook updates, prioritized action list with owners and target dates.

QBR Metrics Template (minimum):
- Total API calls, total tokens generated, average cost per 1k tokens, 7/30/90d retention and active endpoints, error rate (4xx/5xx), latency percentiles (P50/P95/P99), availability % (SLA).

Known Issues & Workarounds (example entries):
- Issue: Tokenization mismatch in customer pre-processing causing truncated responses. Workaround: Align tokenizer to model family; provide pre-processing snippet: replace non-UTF8 chars and normalize whitespace.
- Issue: Elevated P99 latency during cold KV cache windows. Workaround: Enable prefix caching and schedule warm-up traffic before peak hours.
- Issue: Occasional function-calling JSON schema errors. Workaround: Validate JSON schema client-side and sanitize outputs with schema enforcement layer.
- Issue: Private deployment: TLS handshake failures with older client stacks. Workaround: Upgrade client TLS library to 1.2+, or enable legacy cipher suite temporarily via SE-approved config.

Support Process (detailed):
- Ticket intake: All customer issues open in Zendesk with tags (customer:<org>, product:inference, env:prod/staging, severity).
- Triage: Support L1 validates customer context and attempts known-workaround. Provide initial update within SLA window.
- Escalation: Use escalation flow above. Add "escalate:yes" tag on Zendesk when moving to SE/Tier2.
- Communication: CSM owns external comms for P1/P2; Support posts internal status updates in the ticket and on the incident channel.

Templates & Attachments:
- Kickoff agenda (copy & paste):
  1) Introductions & roles
  2) Success criteria & timeline
  3) Network & security checklist
  4) Integration walkthrough (SE demo)
  5) Monitoring & alerting
  6) Next steps
- QBR slide template: Executive summary slide, usage & performance slide, roadmap & asks slide, action-items slide. (Deck stored in /confluence/sales-enablement/pitch-decks).

Operational Metrics & Dashboards to provision:
- Per-route token usage (daily/weekly)
- Cost by model and customer (per-token)
- Error rates (4xx/5xx) and top error messages
- Latency percentiles by model and endpoint
- Cache hit rate and batching efficiency metrics

Postmortem & Continuous Improvement:
- Postmortem required for Sev1/Sev2 incidents with customer impact. Must include timeline, RCA, action owner, and verification plan. Publish summary to customer within 7 days and internal RCA within 14 days.
- Quarterly operational review between CS and Product to feed back recurring issues and feature requests.

Appendix — Useful Commands & Links:
- Status page: https://status.redwood.ai
- Debug bundle command: redwood-cli collect-logs --help
- Standard SLA language reference: /confluence/customer-success-and-support/sla-templates
- On-call rota: /confluence/eng-sre/on-call-schedule

Revision history:
- 2024-10-15: Initial draft (Ava Thompson)
- 2025-06-03: Added network table and escalation SLAs (reviewers: Diego Rivera)
- 2026-02-10: Updated QBR cadence and performance validation steps (reviewers: Priya Patel, Liam O'Connor)

If you are running an onboarding and have additional edge-case needs (air-gapped deployments, special compliance controls, or custom model routing), contact the Private Deployments team and attach the customer requirements doc to the onboarding spreadsheet.
